info.name: Egoola API — Attributes & Listing SKUs
info.description: Attribute / Attribute Value management (Size, Colour ... and their values) and listing SKUs: one SKU per option combination, each with its own price, discount window and stock. Admin-only. Run **Auth → Admin Login** first, then the folders in order. See docs/attribute-sku-guide.md.

request.description: Public endpoint — no token needed. Returns access + refresh JWTs carrying actor_type=admin. Every Brand and Listing endpoint below is Admin-only.
Exchanges the saved refresh token (14-day life) for a new access token (1-hour life). Run this instead of logging in again once the access token expires.
`name` is required and unique (any letter case). `name_bn`, `description` and `description_bn` are optional. `is_active` defaults to true.
Names are unique regardless of upper/lower case.

item.name: Create attribute — spare one for the delete demo

request.description: Not used by any listing, so it can be deleted at the end.
`?name=` is a case-insensitive substring. `?search=` also matches the Bangla name. `?is_active=true|false`. Every attribute lists its `values`.

item.name: Create value — Colour Red (with Bangla name)
Create value under the spare attribute
Create value — duplicate in the same attribute (expect 400)

request.description: A value name is unique inside its attribute (any letter case). The same name under another attribute is fine.
Filters: `?attribute=` (id), `?name=` (substring), `?is_active=`. `?search=` also matches the Bangla name.
A value cannot be moved to another attribute: SKUs already point at it.

item.name: Create listing with 4 SKUs (Size x Colour)

request.description: Price, discount and stock live on the SKU. Each SKU has one `variants` row per attribute: `{attribute, attribute_value}` ids. All SKUs of a listing must use the same attributes, and no two SKUs can have the same combination. The listing-level `price` / `discounted_price` in the response are read-only: the cheapest active SKU.

exec: pm.test("each SKU has 2 variant rows", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().skus.every(s => s.variants.length === 2)).to.eql(true));
pm.test("listing from-price = cheapest SKU", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.price).to.eql('1800.00'); pm.expect(b.discounted_price).to.eql('1500.00'); });

item.name: Create listing — no skus and no price (expect 400)

request.description: A listing needs at least one SKU: send `skus`, or `price` for a single default SKU.

item.name: Add a new SKU (Size S + Green)

request.description: `skus` on update merges by id: an item without `id` creates a SKU; SKUs you do not mention are left alone. SKUs are never deleted.

item.name: Update a SKU by id — price (discount follows)

request.description: Only the fields you send change. A SKU with no discount follows a new price; a discounted SKU keeps its discount.

exec: pm.test("no-discount SKU follows the price", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().skus.find(s => s.id == pm.collectionVariables.get('sku_m_blue')).discounted_price).to.eql('2000.00'));

item.name: Update a SKU by id — stock only
Update a SKU by id — discount window

request.description: The discount only applies between `discount_start_date` and `discount_end_date` (either can be empty = no limit). Outside the window the buyer pays `price`; `effective_price` shows what is charged right now and `is_discount_active` says whether the discount applies.

exec: pm.test("window over: effective price is the normal price", () => { const s = pm.response.json().skus.find(x => x.id == pm.collectionVariables.get('sku_l_blue')); pm.expect(s.effective_price).to.eql('1900.00'); pm.expect(s.is_discount_active).to.eql(false); pm.expect(s.discounted_price).to.eql('1500.00'); });

item.name: Update a SKU by id — replace its options

request.description: When `variants` is sent for an existing SKU it replaces that SKU's options; when it is left out the options stay.

item.name: Deactivate a SKU (hide it from the storefront)

request.description: SKUs are never deleted, because carts and orders point at them. Hide one with `is_active: false`; the storefront should skip inactive SKUs.

exec: pm.test("still returned but inactive", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().skus.find(s => s.id == pm.collectionVariables.get('sku_m_red')).is_active).to.eql(false));

item.name: Update — SKUs with different attribute sets (expect 400)

request.description: Every SKU of a listing has to use the same attributes (all Size + Colour here).

item.name: Update — value of the wrong attribute (expect 400)
Update — SKU id from another listing (expect 400)
Update — price shortcut on an existing listing (expect 400)

request.description: The plain `price` shortcut only works when creating. Change prices through `skus`.

item.name: Price tier tied to a SKU (listing_sku)

request.description: Quantity tiers still apply to the whole listing. `listing_sku` is optional and, when sent, must be a SKU of this listing.

exec: pm.test("first tier tied to the SKU", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().price_tiers[0].listing_sku).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('sku_m_blue'))));

item.name: Create a simple listing with the price shortcut

request.description: Without options, send `price` (and optionally `discounted_price`, `discount_start_date`, `discount_end_date`, `stock_qty`, `sku`) and one default SKU is created for you. Do not send both this and `skus`.

exec: pm.test("price, discount and stock on the SKU", () => { const s = pm.response.json().skus[0]; pm.expect([s.price, s.discounted_price, s.stock_qty]).to.eql(['100.00','80.00',7]); });

item.name: Delete an attribute that is in use (expect 409)

request.description: An attribute or value used by a listing SKU cannot be deleted. Deactivate it with `is_active: false` instead.

item.name: Delete a value that is in use (expect 409)

request.description: A soft-deleted listing still keeps its SKUs, so its attributes stay in use and cannot be deleted; deactivate them so they leave the dropdowns.
